the normal high tide line, peaking during high tide.

* WHERE...Eastern Norton Sound and Nulato Hills.

* WHEN...From 10 AM Thursday to 4 AM AKDT Friday.

* IMPACTS...Localized beach erosion may occur.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...A low in the Western Bering Sea will send a
front moving East in the coast, resulting in south to southeast
winds ramping up Thursday morning through Friday, before
diminishing through Saturday. Sea levels will remain elevated
through Friday before gradually subsiding Friday night into
Saturday.

properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued October 5 at 10:24AM ChST by NWS Tiyan GU
properties.description:
UPDATED to account for Invest 94W becoming TD 27W.

...HEAVY SHOWERS, GUSTY WINDS, AND CHOPPY SEAS LIKELY THE NEXT FEW
DAYS ACROSS THE NORTHERN MARSHALL ISLANDS DOWN TO MAJURO...

A developing disturbance known as Invest 94W by the Joint Typhoon
Warning Center (JTWC) is located about 140 miles southwest of
Utirik. Scatterometry data indicates 15 to 20 kt winds near
Kwajalein, Ebadon, Ujae, Bikini, and Rongelap, with winds up to 25 kt
near heavier showers. TD 27W will be generally slow to move,
remaining over the northern Marshall Islands through Tuesday night.
Scattered to numerous showers and isolated thunderstorms may lead to
locally heavy rainfall and flooding. Through Friday, 4 to 6 inches of
rain with locally higher amounts are possible.

Gusty winds and elevated, choppy seas will make marine conditions
difficult. Residents may need to reconsider plans for inter-island
boating as the week continues.

27W will continue to develop near Kwajalein over the next day or
two, so residents in the northern Republic of Marshall Islands (RMI)
should monitor the forecast for the next several days.

For more information on Invest 94W please see the Significant Tropical
Weather Advisory from the Joint Typhoon Warning Center under WMO
header ABPW10 PGTW. Also keep up to date with the latest information
from your local emergency management agency.
